Definition: a kind of lizard (from its covert habits)
BiblicalUsage: lᵉṭâʼâh means a kind of lizard — a small word with a sharp edge. In Leviticus 11:30, "and the lizard".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the lizard on the unclean list reminds me that God drew lines His people were meant to keep — even over the small creeping things.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
